decisions.statement: A deploy that runs in the cluster runs as a job of its own.
A job is named for the subject deployed and the commit it is made at.
A job takes the repository from the git service inside the cluster.
The token a job reads the repository with is handed in from a secret.
The key a job decrypts a secret with is handed in from a secret.
No token is written into the job the cluster is handed.
A job fetches the commit it is made at rather than the whole history.
A job builds no index, git carrying every index a page is read through.
A job runs in the image a pipeline's own steps run in.
A job runs on a node of the class that carries this work.
A job that failed is not run again by the cluster.
The deploy a job carries runs under no ceiling of the command's own.
A job bounds the deploy it carries, and nothing inside that deploy does.
The memory a landing starts on is read from the pod rather than the workstation.
The command the job runs is asked of the index rather than spelled.
Nothing here applies the job to the cluster.
Nothing here reads the workstation's checkout.
A job runs under no syscall filter.
The overlay a job's test gate mounts is held on a volume of the job's own.
A job states that the run it carries is the one in the cluster.
A job fetches the commit its subject was last deployed at beside the commit it is made at.
A job whose subject was never deployed fetches one commit.
A last deployed commit origin no longer carries leaves the rest of the job running.
A job holds every privilege the node gives a container.
A job makes control groups of its own under the one it runs in.

definition: the job a deploy runs as, checked out in the cluster at the commit it is made at
